title: Adaptations to environment
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: Can you give me an example of a structural adaptation?
What is the difference between structural and physiological adaptations?
Do animals have behavioural adaptations too?

explain.say: Today we are learning about adaptations to the environment.

items: These changes suit a specific environment.

explain.say: First we look at structural adaptations. These are body parts that help an organism live.
Next we study behavioural adaptations. These are actions or ways an animal acts to survive.
Then we cover physiological adaptations. These are internal body processes that help an organism cope.
For example, a camel has structural adaptations like humps for fat storage.
A polar bear's thick layer of blubber is a structural adaptation for cold water.

faq.q: What is the difference between structural and physiological adaptations?
faq.a: Structural adaptations involve physical body parts, like a long beak. Physiological adaptations involve internal body processes, such as how an animal digests food.
asks: What counts as a physiological change?

faq.q: Can a behaviour be both structural and physiological?
faq.a: No, they are distinct types. Behaviour is an action, while structural relates to fixed body parts, and physiological relates to internal workings.

faq.q: Are plants included when we talk about adaptations?
faq.a: Yes, plants show all three types. For instance, a cactus has structural spines, and roots are physiological.
asks: How do plants adapt to dry land?

faq.q: Do all adaptations help an organism survive?
faq.a: Yes, adaptations are traits that increase the chance of survival and reproduction in a specific environment over time.
asks: What happens if an adaptation is not helpful?

faq.q: Does the environment change over time?
faq.a: Yes, changes in the environment cause natural selection, leading to new adaptations over many generations.

facts: Structural adaptations are physical features of an organism.
Behavioural adaptations are actions taken by an animal.
Physiological adaptations are internal life processes.
Adaptations help species survive in their specific habitat.

quiz.say: A fish having gills to breathe underwater is an example of:
quiz.why: Gills are a fixed, physical body part that allows the fish to breathe water.

wrong.0: Behavioural refers to actions, not body parts.
wrong.1: Physiological refers to internal processes, not visible structures.
wrong.2: Habitat is the place where the organism lives, not the adaptation itself.

quiz.say: A bird flying south when winter approaches is an example of:
quiz.why: Migration is an action or pattern of movement, which is a behaviour.

wrong.1: Structural adaptations are parts of the body, not actions.
wrong.2: Physiological relates to internal functions like digestion.
wrong.3: This is too general; we need to specify the type of adaptation.

quiz.say: A lizard absorbing salts through its skin is an example of:
quiz.why: Absorbing salts through the skin is an internal, chemical process happening in the body.

wrong.1: Structural adaptations involve visible, fixed body parts.
wrong.2: Behavioural relates to actions like basking or hiding.
wrong.3: An exoskeleton is a structure, not the process of absorption.
